So, the -- I would say 30% of the production will be productionized by FY 28 and another 50% will come into FY 29, I would say.
Growth & demand: Aluminium, we are on a growth path, and this growth journey will continue.

The aluminium segment's pace of growth or the absolute growth and even percentage growth, all of that will beat the other segments that is clear because of the massive investments which has gone in the recent past.
But also, we see big improvement in the revenue growth, revenue growth even after adjusting the aluminium cost, we are seeing higher traction in the growth.
Margins & costs: Once we see that we are crossing this 80% threshold, we are marginally expanding the capacity.
The current EBIT margins of the current Powertrain business is having a weightage of more than 70%, 75% on investments made on the conventional powertrain, I would say.

But we have to understand when the new capacity is coming up with a larger capacity and capacity utilization is lesser, the EBIT margins may look depressed on that particular portion for some time until capacity utilization and operating leverage sets up.
Capex & expansion: So, on a consolidated basis for this year, should we work with about INR 1,500 crores of capex, subject to obviously, revisions depending on capacity utilization in the second half.

So, when you want to go for a plant of a decent size, not mega size, I think the land and building and infrastructure, the ETP, HTP, the power connections and the road infrastructure there, will touch around INR 150 crores to INR 250 crores, depending on the plant size.
So, any greenfield project, anywhere between INR 100 crores to INR 250 crores will be the basic infrastructure without the production equipment to have a plant readiness to accept the equipment.
Balance sheet & cash: So, the operating leverage is helping us to increase the margins.
So, when we're exiting this, I think surely, the margins will pick up with the better operating leverage from new customers which are coming in.
So , this will have -- unless we fill up the plant with a decent amount of production capacity, the operating leverage will not set in.
Risks & challenges: It is for the additional high- pressure die casting and to start with high-pressure die casting only on parts which are for the automotive industry.
So, the biggest challenge about the customers accepting us as a supplier, first of all, and because their product quality depends on us.
I think beyond 75% is very difficult because of the seasonal nature of the business and the risk of stopping customer lines.

guidance.t: So, exit rate, I'm very confident about Q4 mid-teens sort of an EBITDA margin for Sunbeam.

The net debt-to-EBITDA is 2.46, and EBITDA margins are around 15%, EBIT margins around 10%, and ROC annualized is 15%.
The H1 revenue is around INR 158 crores and we had an EBITDA of around INR 14.87 crores, EBIT of around INR 11.4 crores.
Capex & expansion: The new CAPEX, the minimum threshold level will be a pre-tax ROC of 20%.
The new CAPEX actually spoils the old return of investment, but the new CAPEX when it starts to mature, then and we slow down investment, I think we will breach even the 20% ROCE levels.

I think we are not breaking the revenue on the alloy wheel, but the plant capacity the installed in total will be 5.8 million between Bhiwadi and Hosur as of now, another 2 million will go to phase-II which is to be installed in the coming couple of quarters at the Hosur plant.
Balance sheet & cash: Now on the “Financial Metrics”: The net debt to EBITDA on the consolidated basis is 0.94.
And your net debt has gone up to INR 2,800 crores.
This will be a process which will go more through the middle of the next financial year and that will reduce the debt of Sunbeam and Craftsman Group as a whole.
Risks & challenges: Only thing the CV has shown a decline and tractor has shown a small increase.
So, I think the changes in the or the slowdown in the commercial vehicle segment is really not affecting us to a level where it affects our profitability.
Commercial vehicle from 49% has declined to 46%, off-highway has increased from 20% to 21%, tractor has increased from 17% to 19% and the SUV segment is flat at 14%.

guidance.t: I think we are looking at double-digit EBITDA margin for the financial year ‘27.
